title: Unit Econ: regional slab simulation extract
content:
WORKING SHEET — external API unit economics by region and slab

PURPOSE
Quick, exportable simulation for per-1k-token COGS and margin across region/model/slab setups. Intended to feed a short recommendations memo (see notes) and a follow-up detailed spreadsheet for CFO review. This is intentionally compact and contains heuristics used in the product team's early-stage tradeoffs.

ASSUMPTIONS (editable)
- GPU amortization: USD per-GPU-hour baked into slab cost input (column).
- Network/transit: estimated per-region egress per 1k tokens applied separately (row-level override allowed).
- Model kernel efficiency: a factor (0.6–1.1) applied to raw perf numbers to capture compilation differences.
- Continuous batching applied at runtime; effective batch factor = min(configured_batch, observed_concurrency).
- KV prefix cache applied at 0–60% hit rates in scenarios.
- Pricing baseline: list price per 1k tokens we want to test vs. slab-sensitive pricing.

TABLE: regional slab sim (columns)
Columns: MODEL | REGION | SLAB_TIER | GPU_COST_per_hour_USD | AMORT_PER_1K_TOKENS_USD | NETWORK_PER_1K_USD | KERNEL_EFF_FACTOR | AVG_TOKENS_PER_REQ | REQS_PER_MIN | BATCH_FACTOR | CACHE_HIT_RATE_pct | EFFECTIVE_COGS_per_1k_USD | PRICE_per_1k_USD | GROSS_MARGIN_pct | NOTES

Rows:
Redwood-Serve-13B | us-west1 | small-slab | 3.50 | 0.045 | 0.008 | 0.95 | 420 | 350 | 1.6 | 12 | 0.056 | 0.120 | 53.3 | baseline small-slab, low cache
OpenChat-7B-lite | eu-west1 | medium-slab | 5.00 | 0.030 | 0.010 | 0.88 | 220 | 120 | 2.8 | 28 | 0.034 | 0.100 | 66.0 | medium-slab benefits from batching
Llama2-70B-opt | ap-southeast1 | large-slab | 11.75 | 0.210 | 0.015 | 1.05 | 680 | 95 | 1.2 | 8 | 0.235 | 0.350 | 32.9 | high amortization, high network
Redwood-Serve-13B-q4 | us-east1 | burst-slab | 7.20 | 0.090 | 0.009 | 0.92 | 420 | 520 | 3.2 | 36 | 0.061 | 0.095 | 35.8 | burst slab with quantization savings

EXTRACTION LOGIC (how EFFECTIVE_COGS_per_1k_USD computed)
- amort per 1k tokens estimated = (GPU_COST_per_hour_USD * hours_per_minute_cost_profile * (avg_tokens_per_req * reqs_per_min / 1000)) / effective_utilization_adjuster
- network added linearly per 1k tokens (NETWORK_PER_1K_USD)
- kernel_eff_factor multiplies amort to capture lower/higher op counts
- cache reduction: EFFECTIVE_COGS *= (1 - CACHE_HIT_RATE_pct / 100) + hit_miss_overhead (small fixed overhead ~0.002)
- batch_factor reduces amort proportionally to sqrt(batch_factor) for conservative estimate (empirical fit from infra traces)

SCENARIOS (quick toggles to copy into a full workbook)
- Baseline: batch_factor = observed, cache_hit_rate = observed
- Batch-first: force batch_factor to 4.0 where supported -> shows large benefits on medium/large models in high-concurrency zones
- Cache-heavy: set cache_hit_rate = 50% across conversational workloads -> highlights aggressively cached instruction-following flows
- Latency-first: cap batch_factor <=1.5, reduce cache to 10% (simulate strict latency SLOs)

EXAMPLE SENSITIVITY OUTPUT (extracted snapshots):
Scenario: Baseline -> Average effective COGS across rows = 0.096 USD per 1k tokens, weighted gross margin at current list prices = 44%
Scenario: Batch-first -> Average effective COGS = 0.068 USD per 1k tokens, weighted gross margin = 56% (biggest wins on eu & us-east medium-slab)
Scenario: Cache-heavy -> Average effective COGS = 0.074 USD per 1k tokens, weighted gross margin = 53%
Scenario: Latency-first -> Average effective COGS = 0.135 USD per 1k tokens, weighted gross margin = 21%

OBSERVATIONS (working bullets)
- Batch improvements produce non-linear savings for medium-slab profiles: pushing batching to supported limits yields 25–40% lower amort per 1k.
- Regions with high GPU hour costs (APAC large-slab) are highly sensitive to price and model choice; recommend model pinning or fallback to smaller variants in ap-southeast.
- Cache yields big wins for chat-heavy conversational customers; for instruction-only workloads the hit-rate assumptions should be reduced by ~60% (short prompts).
- Burst slabs are useful for short spikes but amortization per-1k jumps if average utilization below ~45% — use burst only for <30-minute spikes or tie to reserved-backed burst credits.

RECOMMENDATIONS (actionable, prioritized)
1) Implement a regional slab recommendation page in the onboarding flow: suggest smaller-slab + batch-first for low-cost regions; recommend dedicated large-slab for stable, high-concurrency enterprise tenants in EU/US. Priority: high. Owner: Product-Optimize.
2) Add a runtime feature flag allowing ops to 'aggressively batch' eligible routes for customers who accept 50–100ms latency variance. Priority: medium. Owner: Serving-Runtime.
3) Pilot a cache-based pricing SKU for conversational customers: discounted per-token price if they accept a 30% expected cache hit minimum (audit logs to validate). Priority: medium-high. Owner: GTM + Product.
4) Regional routing rules: prefer models with lower amortization in APAC by default; fallback to smaller quantized variants when large-slab costs exceed threshold. Priority: medium. Owner: Smart-Routing team.

OPEN QUESTIONS
- What is a defensible threshold for 'burst-slab' acceptance in enterprise contracts? (legal + finance input needed)
- Can we instrument more accurate kernel_eff_factor per model family in the next infra release?

TO DO / NEXT STEPS
- [ ] Convert to detailed workbook with per-minute utilization traces (JIRA-OPT-987).
- [ ] Run Monte Carlo 10k sims across request mix distributions and add 95% CI bands.
- [ ] Sync with Finance to align amortization methodology (deadline: 2026-02-05).
- [ ] Draft short customer-facing guidance doc to be used by Solutions Engineering for cost optimization consultations.

QUICK NOTES FOR CFO-STYLE SLICE (one-paragraph)
This extract demonstrates that batching and caching are the highest-leverage levers for improving per-token margins for the External API. Under realistic traffic mixes, enabling moderate batching and 25–35% cache hit rates can shift blended per-1k token COGS down by ~25–35%, unlocking margin recovery without price increases. Regions with high GPU-hour slabs (APAC large) should be targeted for model pinning and fallback routing to protect margins.

REFERENCES / RAW INPUTS
- sample infra trace: s3://infra-traces/2025-11/top-50k-requests.csv
- prior optimization brief: CONFLUENCE-9876 (internal)

END OF EXTRACT - save as JSON export and copy into product/optimize workbook for deeper analysis
